definitions.gloss: penniless; broke; without a cent; flat broke
definitions.explanation: Having no money at all. Literally means not even one mon (an old unit of currency). Used to describe a state of complete financial emptiness.

examples.japanese: {無一文|むいちもん}になってしまった。
⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{無一文|むいちもん}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{会社|かいしゃ}→会社：00607_kaisha⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{立|た}ち{上|あ}げた→立ち上げる：07892_tachiageru⟧。
examples.english: He started the company from nothing.

examples.japanese: ⟦ギャンブル→ギャンブル：10811_gyanburu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{手|て}→手：00569_te⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{出|だ}して→出す：01087_dasu⟧{無一文|むいちもん}になった⟦{友人|ゆうじん}→友人：03649_yuujin⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{何度|なんど}→何度：17592_nando⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{見|み}て→見る：00283_miru⟧きた。
examples.english: I've seen many friends go broke from getting into gambling.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{無|む}→無：17750_mu⟧ (without) + {一文|いちもん} (one mon — the smallest old coin denomination). Literally means not having even one mon. The ⟦{文|もん}→文：29590_mon⟧ was a very small unit of currency in pre-modern Japan, so the expression emphasizes total poverty.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {無一文|むいちもん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧ (to become penniless)
- {無一文|むいちもん}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{始|はじ}める (to start from nothing)
- {無一文|むいちもん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{状態|じょうたい}→状態：03345_joutai⟧ (a state of being penniless)
- {無一文|むいちもん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{放|ほう}り{出|だ}される→放り出す：16163_houridasu⟧ (to be thrown out without a penny)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {一文無|いちもんな}し — penniless; an older variant with essentially the same meaning
- {文無|もんな}し — penniless; colloquial variant
- ⟦{金欠|きんけつ}→金欠：14442_kinketsu⟧ — short of cash; more casual and less extreme, implying temporary shortage
- すっからかん — completely broke; very colloquial and emphatic

ETYMOLOGY:
The ⟦{文|もん}→文：29590_mon⟧ was the smallest unit of currency during the Edo period. Even one ⟦{文|もん}→文：29590_mon⟧ had very little value, so saying someone doesn't have even one emphasizes the completeness of their poverty.
